Goal is for viewers to be able to join top tier labs (OpenAI, Google, MIT) or publish cutting edge open source research & code models. Introduction & Motivation Python for Machine Learning: From Simple to Advanced Attention Mechanism Tutorial: From Simple to Advanced Chapter 1 Chapter 2
(I need to put this somewhere, probably towards the end or in research part) (paaraphrasing Keller Jordan, I will shorten or move this somewhere else): We need a dedicated to AI model speedruns—structured competitions where researchers must train tiny LLMs or similar models under strict constraints. The goal is to create a fair environment where new methods (like optimizers or architectures) can be tested against fully optimized baselines. Without this, many research get "state-of-the-art" results simply because they didn't optimize existing methods to their limits, and not because their new idea is better. This is wasting a lot of time for other researchers and teams who implement the method and find out it's not actually better. It can also motivate companies like OpenAI and Google to open source algorithms they want optimized by open source community. entry.title: 🧠 Title: Building Your Developer Brand in 2025: Why Code Alone Isn’t Enough
entry.summary: 🧠 Title: Building Your Developer Brand in 2025: Why Code Alone Isn’t Enough Hey devs 👋 In 2025, being a great developer is about more than just shipping clean code. It’s about visibility, communication, and trust. Whether you’re job-hunting, freelancing, building a SaaS, or contributing to open source, one thing’s clear: 👨‍💻 Why You Need a Developer Brand It’s about making it easy for people to: Find your work Understand your strengths Trust your expertise In short: your GitHub, blog, portfolio, and posts tell a story. What story are you telling? 🔧 Tools of the Trade: Build a Digital Presence That Works While You Sleep Pin meaningful projects Write clean, well-documented READMEs Contribute to open source, even small things (PRs, typo fixes) DEV.to / Hashnode / Personal Blog (Your Voice) Write dev diaries, tutorials, or lessons learned Share solutions to common bugs or obscure issues Post about your side projects or experiments LinkedIn or Twitter (Your Network) Share your wins, challenges, and insights Connect with devs in your stack Be human, not a spam bot Portfolio Site (Your Landing Page) Keep it simple: who you are, what you do, how to contact you Link to GitHub, blog, resume 💡 Content Ideas for Dev Blogging (Yes, Even If You're “Not a Writer”) “A Beginner’s Guide to X I Wish Existed” “Building Y with Z: My Honest Experience” “5 VS Code Extensions I Can’t Live Without” “How I Prepared for My First Tech Interview” You don’t need to be fancy. Just be helpful. Be real. ✅ TL;DR Don’t just build. Document. Don’t just code. Communicate. Don’t just exist. Be discoverable. Your digital brand doesn’t have to be big — it just has to be authentic and visible. Let your code speak. But don’t forget to tell your story too. ✍️ Written by BADUSH MUHAMMED , DIGITAL MARKETING EXPERT IN KOTTAYAM https://badushmuhammed.com
